scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: A support call
scenes.caption: In a classroom role-play, Kavya receives a call claiming to be account support. The caller says her school account will close unless she reads out a login code. No actual account or code appears anywhere in the activity.

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: Different secrets
scenes.caption: Her teacher introduces three labelled cards. A password protects account access. A one-time password, or OTP, confirms a particular action for a limited period. A UPI PIN authorises payment actions. Calling all three just a number hides their different purposes.
scenes.dialogue: Read the purpose, not the digits.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: The caller’s request
scenes.caption: The pretend notification says the OTP is for signing in. Sharing it could help another person complete that sign-in. The caller’s claimed job does not change the code’s purpose, and Kavya does not need to investigate or challenge the caller.
scenes.dialogue: End the call and get help.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: Choose the response
scenes.caption: Kavya can read the code aloud, send a screenshot, or end the call and ask a trusted adult to open the service’s previously known help route. Choose a response that keeps the secret away from another person.
scenes.dialogue: A screenshot shares the secret too.

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: A legitimate sign-in
scenes.caption: Later, Kavya intentionally opens the school’s verified sign-in page with her teacher. Its stated action matches the login she initiated. Entering the requested OTP there is different from sending it to a caller or a message link.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: An unexpected code
scenes.caption: The lab changes the situation: an OTP arrives when nobody requested a sign-in. Build a code-handling record that leaves it unused, avoids forwarding it and asks for account checks through trusted support.
